nodes.label: Chunking Types for Text Processing
nodes.description: Different strategies for splitting text into smaller, manageable units, often used in NLP and RAG systems.

nodes.label: Fixed-size Chunking
nodes.description: Splits text into equal token or character lengths.

nodes.label: How It Works
nodes.description: Splits text into equal token/char lengths (e.g., 512 tokens, 50 overlap).

nodes.label: Cons / Trade-offs
nodes.description: Breaks sentences mid-thought, loses semantic meaning.

nodes.label: Production Use Case
nodes.description: Baseline for unstructured text or fast prototyping.

nodes.label: Recursive Chunking
nodes.description: Splits text along natural boundaries until the desired size is met.

nodes.label: How It Works
nodes.description: Splits along natural boundaries (paragraph → sentence → word) until size fits.

nodes.label: Semantic Chunking
nodes.description: Uses NLP to split text by meaning units.

nodes.label: How It Works
nodes.description: Uses NLP to split by meaning units (sections, headings, paragraphs).

nodes.label: Hierarchical Chunking
nodes.description: Involves multi-level chunking for flexible retrieval granularity.

nodes.label: Metadata-enriched Chunking
nodes.description: Attaches additional information (metadata) to chunks to improve context and governance.

nodes.label: How It Works
nodes.description: Attaches metadata (source, date, author, lineage) to chunks.

nodes.label: Pros
nodes.description: Boosts accuracy up to 5×, supports governance.

nodes.label: Agentic / Context-graph Chunking
nodes.description: Builds a graph of chunks with semantic links for advanced retrieval.

nodes.label: How It Works
nodes.description: Builds graph of chunks with semantic links.
